Playground is an American cloud-based software as a service (SaaS) platform for the management of early childhood education and childcare programs. The software is designed to consolidate administrative functions — including billing, enrollment, attendance tracking, family communication, digital paperwork, and payroll — into a single platform for childcare centers, home-based providers, and multi-site organizations.
Playground is operated by Carline Inc., a privately held company. The platform has been adopted through state-funded programs in Iowa, Kansas, Texas, and other U.S. states.
Co-founders Daniel Andrews, Josh Andrews, and Sasha Reiss were named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in the Education category in 2023.
Product
Playground is a cloud-based childcare management platform. Its features include automated billing and tuition collection, digital enrollment and registration, attendance tracking with sign-in and sign-out functionality, family communication tools, digital paperwork and document storage, subsidy tracking, food program reporting for the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), and payroll processing.
According to Child Care Aware of Kansas, the platform is designed to reduce administrative burden for childcare providers by automating recurring tasks such as billing reminders, enrollment workflows, and document collection. The platform pre-populates state-required licensing documents for providers in participating states at sign-up.
The Texas Family Child Care Network, a program funded by the Texas Workforce Commission, describes Playground as operable from any device including mobile phones, and lists billing, attendance, payroll, registration, communications, and paperwork management among its core functions.
Government adoption
Iowa
In October 2022, Early Childhood Iowa and the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) launched a Shared Services initiative pairing Playground with financial management coaching for childcare providers across the state. Under the program, the State of Iowa funded monthly subscription fees for providers to use either Playground or its competitor brightwheel, originally for a period of 12 months, later extended through September 2024.
The Iowa program also offered technology grants of up to $1,000 per provider to support implementation of the software. In February 2023, Iowa HHS launched a direct data bridge connecting Playground to KinderTrack (KT), the state's child care subsidy data system, enabling providers to submit child attendance data electronically to receive Child Care Assistance (CCA) reimbursements without manual data entry.
As of the July 2023 Iowa HHS project update, hundreds of Iowa childcare providers — including both child development homes and childcare centers — had enrolled in the program.
Kansas
Child Care Aware of Kansas, a nonprofit organization affiliated with Child Care Aware of America, offered free 24-month subscriptions to Playground for licensed childcare providers in Kansas as part of a state-supported provider assistance initiative. The Kansas program included pre-configured state licensing documents within providers' Playground accounts at sign-up.
Texas
The Texas Family Child Care Network (Texas FCCN), a statewide initiative funded by a grant from the Texas Workforce Commission under RFA 32025-00067, offered 500 free one-year subscriptions to Playground — alongside competitor Brightwheel — for eligible permitted family childcare providers in Texas. The program also included up to three hours of personalized setup support per provider. The Texas FCCN noted that the Texas Workforce Commission did not specifically endorse any particular platform, and participation was at providers' discretion. The Texas FCCN is additionally supported by the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
Recognition
In 2023, co-founders Daniel Andrews and Sasha Reiss were included on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in the Education category. The 30 Under 30 list is an annually published editorial selection by Forbes recognizing individuals under the age of 30 in various industries.
